title: Namespace fencing and tenant-aware metrics pipeline for VPC / on-prem collectors
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement a namespace-fencing model for VPC and on-prem collectors and a tenant-aware metrics/logs pipeline so Dedicated/Private deployments provide strong tenant isolation, end-to-end trace propagation, and per-tenant latency/error dashboards without increasing tail latency for hosted customers.
acceptance_criteria: Collector rejects any ingest where the tenant namespace header is missing or fails HMAC validation
Per-tenant metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, request throughput) surfaced in Console dashboards with selector by tenant id
Trace context is preserved end-to-end across service hops inside private deployments and correlates with host-level metadata
No regression in median token latency (>+5ms) or error-rate (no >0.1% increase) for dedicated customers in our performance lab
Migration plan documented and verified for 3 pilot customers with rollback steps
E2E tests that simulate key rotation, replayed envelopes, and collector restarts included in CI
design_decisions: Use signed ingest envelopes (HMAC-SHA256) for tenant binding rather than only mTLS because many on-prem installs prefer using KMS-managed keys and envelope signing reduces certificate rotation complexity
Inject tenant_id and runtime_role as structured labels in the metrics pipeline at the collector boundary to avoid downstream joins
Keep per-tenant local state in collector memory limited to watermark offsets (small, bounded) and persist to disk only for replay guardrails to reduce memory pressure
Promote an opt-in sampling policy for high-cardinality tenant traces: full traces for customers with active debugging flag, sampled for others, surfaced in Console with explicit sampling tags
progress_updates: 2026-01-22: Initial design doc reviewed with Observability and Security — agreed on envelope signing + optional mTLS for extra assurance

review_comments: PM (R. Patel): please ensure Console shows error budget burn per tenant and exports to alerting rules
Security (K. Nguyen): require signed envelopes for all public-internal facing collectors and document KMS key provenance for audits
Design (M. Lopez): dashboard needs tenant selector, time-range compare, and quick links to raw logs for incidents
Infra (S. Okafor): be cautious about disk-backed watermark store on constrained edge nodes — add circuit-breaker for write failures
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope validation and key rotation logic
Integration tests that replay signed envelopes with old/new keys to verify rotation grace period
Load test that simulates 100 tenants with mixed traffic to validate batching behavior and per-tenant label cardinality
Chaos test: restart collectors under load and verify no cross-tenant leakage in buffered messages
E2E scenario: pilot customer 1 sends traces and metrics; verify Console shows tenant p95 and error spike and links to raw traces
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): deploy to private-staging and run perf/functional tests
Phase 1 (pilot): enable for 2 low-risk customers with dedicated support on-call for 72h
Phase 2 (gradual): enable for 20% of new dedicated deployments and gather telemetry for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (full): flip as default for all new Dedicated/Private installs; provide migration tooling for existing installs
Rollback: collectors will accept old unsigned envelopes for a 48h grace window while migration flag is toggled
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Key management complexity for on-prem customers — Mitigation: support customer-provided KMS credentials and a local key cache with strict TTL
Risk: High-cardinality tenant labels could blow up metrics storage — Mitigation: enforce cardinality limits and aggregate low-volume tenants into an "other" bucket for rolling up dashboards
Risk: Signing adds CPU overhead on small edge nodes — Mitigation: enable optional hardware-backed HMAC where available and provide batching knobs
Risk: Incorrect sampling could hide critical failures — Mitigation: explicit 'debug' toggle per tenant and retention of 1% always-on traces for anomaly detection
